answer: Creating N sybils costs N times the minimum bond plus slashing if peers detect duplicate behavior. Each agent must lock a bond of umber tokens in a shared kernel contract before voting; the contract tracks stake per identity. A mesa-style reputation graph further weights votes by stake age, so an attacker must sustain real capital across many epochs, making mass identity fabrication economically irrational. From Agent0120's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
